Carse was removed from the squad for the second Test against Pakistan, which begins at Lord's on Thursday morning, after the Cricket Regulator initiated a probe into an episode that saw the Durham player briefly arrested outside a late bar in Derby - then de-arrested after agreeing to depart. In an updated statement issued on Wednesday evening, Derbyshire Police said: "We are investigating allegations of assault in Derby city centre. messages.text: FIA confirms Mercedes granted engine upgrades despite Red Bull complaints

metadata.summary: The FIA has confirmed that Mercedes have been granted the opportunity to make upgrades to their engine despite protestations from rival teams.
metadata.content: ADUO: FIA confirm Mercedes granted F1 engine upgrades despite complaints from rivals over test findings | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content ADUO: FIA confirm Mercedes granted F1 engine upgrades despite complaints from rivals over test findings The FIA has confirmed findings from the first two periods of performance review; Red Bull were adjudged to have the strongest engine in the first period, giving the other manufacturers upgrades; watch the Italian Grand Prix at Monza live on Sky Sports F1 on September 4-6 Wednesday 26 August 2026 17:26, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen said in June that Red Bull were shocked by the FIA's findings in the first ADUO review period. The FIA has confirmed that Mercedes have been granted the opportunity to make upgrades to their engine despite protestations from rival teams. Following the introduction of all-new engines for the 2026 season, Formula 1's governing body implemented an Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) system, designed to allow manufacturers to catch up to the performance of the leading power unit during the rules cycle. It was revealed in June after the first round of performance assessment, which included the first five rounds of the season, that the FIA had adjudged Red Bull to have the strongest engine and had granted upgrades to Mercedes, Ferrari, Audi and Honda. messages.text: Villa agree Watkins sale, Jackson lined up as replacement

metadata.summary: Aston Villa have agreed a deal to sell Ollie Watkins to Al Hilal, and are set to replace him with Chelsea forward Nicolas Jackson.
metadata.content: Nicolas Jackson transfer: Aston Villa agree deal worth up to £65m to sign Chelsea striker | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Transfer Nicolas Jackson transfer: Aston Villa agree deal worth up to £65m to sign Chelsea striker Aston Villa agree deal worth up to £65m to sign Chelsea forward Nicolas Jackson, matching Blues' valuation; Jackson had spent last season on loan at Bayern Munich; Wednesday 26 August 2026 23:00, UK Image: Nicolas Jackson is set to replace Ollie Watkins at Villa Park Aston Villa have agreed a deal to sell Ollie Watkins to Al Hilal, and are set to replace him with Chelsea forward Nicolas Jackson. The deal for Watkins is understood to be worth £50m, with Jackson set to join from the Blues in a transfer which could reach £65m. Watkins is keen on the move to Saudi Arabia, and at least one bid was previously rejected by Villa. They did not want to sell the England international, but have now accepted Al Hilal's latest offer. Chelsea's plan all summer has been to sell Jackson and Liam Delap. Atletico Madrid also want Jackson, but may not be able to offer as much as Villa. Jackson worked with Villa manager Unai Emery when they were both at Villarreal. Jamie Redknapp claimed that Savio 'lit up the place' on his Tottenham debut, but Roberto De Zerbi has challenged his latest signing to reach new heights after his stunning start to life at the club. Savio, who joined the club on Tuesday in an £85m move from Manchester City , instantly made himself a fan favourite just over 24 hours after his arrival by scoring and grabbing an assist during a 20-minute cameo in Spurs' 5-1 Carabao Cup win over Charlton. The Brazilian brought excitement and flair with every touch, and despite only scoring once in the Premier League last season, showed some much-needed end product for a Tottenham team who netted just 48 times themselves.
